attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his own newsletter, presented as his blunt view.

semantics.note: Keeps 'every bit', the rough 2025 size of about $65B, the claim that subsidy is the cause, and the counterfactual about a sustainable rate. Calling it causal fits 'only exists due to subsidies'.

contract.note: The plain reading (paid demand for generative AI services, realized 2025 spending, below-cost pricing as the subsidy) is ordinary and fair. The speaker gave no market boundary or accounting basis, so the result depends on those choices.

evidence.note: Menlo Ventures publicizing its own survey-based estimate ($37B enterprise spend, $19B on applications). It covers enterprise only and has no cost data, so it settles neither the $65B total nor dependence on subsidies.

reviews.rationale: The packet has only a partial enterprise-spending estimate. Nothing in it measures total 2025 AI demand on a consistent basis. Nothing shows demand depends on below-cost pricing or disappears at cost-covering prices, and nothing shows it holding up at such prices. The causal claim and the market-size figure are both unsettled.

attribution.note: Zitron's own assessment in his own post.

semantics.note: Faithfully links the $40B one-year debt and the claimed breach of the 25% LTV policy to a 'very precarious' position. Causal is acceptable, though the judgment is largely evaluative.

contract.note: 'Very precarious' has no stated threshold. Reading it as material near-term refinancing vulnerability is fair. Requiring proof of the LTV breach is fair because he asserted it. The result depends on how severe a position must be to count.

evidence.note: SoftBank's own offering memo: the $40B facility matures in March 2027 and $10B was drawn on April 1. It states the LTV policy, but its pro forma LTV figures do not show a breach at March 31.
Bloomberg, March 5: wider CDS spreads and a negative S&P outlook show credit concern before the facility existed. The LTV of 27-28% is an analyst projection, not a confirmed breach.

reviews.rationale: The evidence confirms the facility, its short maturity, and real credit concern. It does not show the $40B was drawn at publication, does not confirm an existing LTV breach, and offers no liquidity analysis that would establish 'very precarious' severity. Unsettled.

attribution.note: Zitron's own prediction in his own post.

semantics.note: 'I wager' works like 'I bet', so this is a scored forecast. It keeps 'first of a few', 'both' companies, and the run-up to S-1 filings.

contract.note: Reading belt-tightening as cuts to access, price rises or operating cuts at both firms, ahead of their filings, is ordinary. 'Few', 'major' and which kind of S-1 counts are unspecified, so the result depends on interpretation.

evidence.note: Anthropic's own announcement of its public S-1 on Oct 26, 2026. It marks Anthropic's filing boundary but says nothing about tightening.
OpenAI's own announcement of a confidential S-1 in June 2026. No public filing yet, and no tightening shown.
TechCrunch, Apr 4: Anthropic moved third-party harness use outside subscription limits. One later tightening at Anthropic only.
Anthropic's own May 6 notice raising and restoring limits. This is an easing, which complicates the predicted pattern without disproving it.

reviews.rationale: There is one documented later tightening at Anthropic, followed by an easing. Nothing documents a major tightening at OpenAI, which has not filed publicly. The early-resolution rule is not met, and the policy record is incomplete, so it cannot show failure either.

attribution.note: Zitron's own conditional prediction in his own post.

semantics.note: The antecedent (ARM below $80) and his own wording 'get hairy' for Son are both kept. 'Going to' is firm wording.

contract.note: Reading 'get hairy' as material pressure on ARM-backed financing is a fair reading in context. The result currently turns on the antecedent not being met, not on that interpretation.

evidence.note: StatMuse price history through Oct 28: the 2026 intraday low was $100.02 on Feb 5, so ARM never traded below $80 after publication. The antecedent is unmet.

reviews.rationale: Through the evaluation date, ARM never traded below $80 after publication, so the condition has not occurred. An unmet antecedent leaves the forecast unscored, not failed. No deadline was stated, so it stays open.
